drivers: one owner (the user) and one release cadence
small scope: four features, six entities
strong consistency between books, ratings and lists (cascading deletes, ownership)
no independent scaling or reliability need per feature
no installs approved; standard library only

alternatives.reason: Shelfie's docs describe catalog/ratings/gateway services, but the code never did this and nothing here needs independent deployment; it would add network calls and split data that must stay consistent
no existing external system has to stay separate
every operation is a synchronous request with an immediate result; no fan-out or background work
no part needs a second style

style.reason: The simplest design that meets every driver; module boundaries keep library, ratings, lists and export separable later.

stack.frontend: Server-rendered HTML (string templates) with a small vanilla JS file for star ratings; no build step
stack.backend: Python 3.10+ standard library: WSGI application (wsgiref in development), sqlite3, hashlib.scrypt, secrets, hmac
stack.hosting: Any host that runs a Python WSGI app; in development the built-in wsgiref server. A production WSGI server (e.g. gunicorn) would be an install that needs approval

reasons.frontend: D10: forms and a few pages; no SPA needed, no toolchain to install
reasons.backend: D02: both sources are standard-library Python; installs are not approved; the app is small enough not to need a framework
reasons.database: D03: both codebases use SQLite (Shelfie's PostgreSQL claim is stale); a single-user-per-row personal app fits a single file
reasons.hosting: D02: no platform constraint given; nothing deploys without approval

modules.name: config
modules.responsibility: Read every setting from environment variables with development defaults; fail clearly on missing secrets outside development

modules.name: accounts
modules.responsibility: Sign up, sign in, sign out, sessions, password hashing, and the can(user, action, record) ownership check

modules.name: library
modules.responsibility: Create, list, view, edit and delete the signed-in user's books

modules.name: ratings
modules.responsibility: Set, change and clear one 1-5 star rating per user per book

modules.name: reading-lists
modules.responsibility: Create, rename, delete and view reading lists; add and remove the user's books

modules.name: export
modules.responsibility: Download the user's library with current ratings as JSON

modules.name: web
modules.responsibility: HTTP shell: routing, cookies, CSRF, JSON error shape, HTML layout and static files

entities.name: Session
entities.primary_key: id text (SHA-256 of the random cookie token)
entities.notes: Expires after 14 days; deleted on sign-out

entities.name: Book
entities.notes: author only existed in Shelfie; owner_id is new

entities.name: Rating
entities.notes: stars 1-5 per the code (docs' 1-10 'score' is stale); upsert replaces append

entities.name: ReadingListItem
entities.notes: Renamed from Readr's ListBook; duplicates now impossible

auth.method: email and password (scrypt hash, per-user salt)
auth.session: server-side Session row; random token in an http-only, SameSite=Lax cookie (Secure in production); 14-day expiry

navigation.screen: Book detail (edit, rate, add to list)

design_system.icons: Unicode stars; no third-party icon set
components: star rating input (radio group, keyboard accessible)

configuration.SESSION_SECRET: signs session and CSRF cookies; required when APP_ENV=production

slices.name: Core loop: sign up, add books, rate them

decisions.decision: Where Shelfie's docs disagree with its code, design from the code (JSON export, 1-5 stars, SQLite, one process)
decisions.reason: User: 'Shelfie's documentation is old; trust what the apps actually do'

decisions.decision: Python 3.10+ standard library only (WSGI, sqlite3, hashlib.scrypt), no third-party packages
decisions.reason: Both sources are stdlib Python; no installs approved; small app

decisions.decision: SQLite with WAL and foreign keys on
decisions.reason: What both codebases actually use; PostgreSQL in Shelfie's README is stale
See style; documented 3-service design was never built and fits no driver

decisions.decision: Email/password accounts with scrypt; server-side sessions in http-only cookies
decisions.reason: Neither source had auth; Shelfie's unused session secret shows sessions were intended

decisions.decision: One role (reader) and per-record ownership enforced by one can() function in every route and query
decisions.reason: Personal libraries; no shared data in any source

decisions.decision: REST JSON under /api/v1; errors {"error":{"code","message"}}; limit/offset paging on list endpoints (default 50, max 200)
decisions.reason: One style, one version scheme, one error shape

decisions.decision: Ratings: integer 1-5, one per user per book, PUT upserts, DELETE clears; API rejects non-integers and booleans; DB CHECK
decisions.reason: Both codebases use 1-5; append-only rows were an integrity bug

decisions.decision: Export: JSON array, one object per book {id,title,author,stars}; CSV not built
decisions.reason: The code exports JSON; CSV exists only in stale docs

decisions.decision: Server-rendered HTML forms plus a small vanilla JS file; JSON API used by the same pages
decisions.reason: No build toolchain to install; accessible by default

decisions.decision: No import of shelfie.db/readr.db data in this plan
decisions.reason: Whether real data exists is unknown; any import is a separate approved migration

decisions.decision: Every feature rebuilt (improve), nothing copied from the sources
decisions.reason: Code reuse is allowed, but the sources are tiny and have the flaws being fixed (no commit, no auth, append ratings)
